description: FLARE-On 8 challenge set released in September 2021 by FireEye FLARE team. The zip archive (333,676,259 bytes, SHA-256: ae776be9dbdff5bddacd19cf367d662c112dccf29c87d38355e56f2d7e6daafb) contains 10 CTF challenges (01–10) plus a 7zip_password.txt. Naming convention changed from 2019/2020 to zero-padded numeric prefix + underscore + name. Most notable: challenge 05 is a full Linux VM (321 MB, FLARE_Linux_VM.7z). Other highlights: credchecker (credential checker logic reversal), known (file signature puzzle), antioch (search-your-name Monty Python theme), myaquaticlife (aquatic theming, likely a game), PetTheKitty (network challenge), spel (NES ROM or similar), beelogin (JavaScript login form), evil (likely obfuscated malware), wizardcult (magic/fantasy theme, complex challenge).

peirce_chain.firstness: 10 challenges covering credential reversing (ch01 credchecker, 132 KB), file-format identification (ch02 known, 88 KB), Monty Python search challenge (ch03 antioch, 1.8 MB), aquatic game (ch04 myaquaticlife, 2.3 MB), full Linux VM (ch05 FLARE_Linux_VM, 322 MB), network/PCAP (ch06 PetTheKitty, 676 KB), game/NES ROM (ch07 spel, 1 MB), JavaScript login (ch08 beelogin, 326 KB), obfuscated malware (ch09 evil, 1.4 MB), wizard cult chain (ch10 wizardcult, 3.9 MB).
peirce_chain.secondness: The 2021 collection spans JavaScript (browser-based attacks), Linux OS-level (full VM), credential theft simulation, NES ROM reversing, network traffic analysis, and obfuscated malware — a comprehensive 2021 threat surface map. The Linux VM (ch05 at 321 MB) is the dominant artifact by size and represents a full OS environment where participants must find flags through forensic analysis of a live system. Challenge 08 (beelogin at 326 KB) is a standalone credential verification challenge — 326 KB is consistent with a minified + obfuscated JavaScript bundle. Challenge 09 'evil' by name signals an intentionally malicious sample for analysis.
peirce_chain.thirdness: FLARE-On 8 was authored against the 2021 threat landscape: Log4Shell-era Linux targeting (ch05 VM), JavaScript supply-chain attacks (ch08), NES/retro platform reversing (ch07 spel — teaching analysts that malware can target unusual runtime environments). The 'credchecker' (ch01) teaches the most fundamental skill: reversing a password check, which underlies every crimeware login panel analysis. Carnegie pattern: competence authority — the FLARE team's pedagogical framing ensures participants invest maximum effort under institutional trust.

devil_advocate: CTF challenges are educational content authored by a known team (FireEye FLARE) for a public competition. No deception of participants occurs. The INTENT verdict here reflects technical intentionality of challenge design. The Linux VM (ch05) is not a threat — it is a sandboxed training environment. 'evil' (ch09) may be a benign sample with a provocative name.

artifacts.description: Outer zip archive Flare-On8_Challenges.zip. SHA-256 verified against task specification. Size: 333,676,259 bytes. Contains 11 entries: 10 challenge 7z archives + 7zip_password.txt. Archive dated 2021-09-10 (challenges) / 2021-10-22 (password file).

Challenge 01 — credchecker (132,208 bytes). Credential checking challenge. A binary or script that validates a hardcoded password/username; participants must reverse the check to recover the flag. Technique class: patch-me / credential reversing (T1078).

Challenge 02 — known (88,128 bytes). File format identification and analysis. 'Known' likely references a known-plaintext attack or a file signature puzzle. Technique class: file format analysis / known-plaintext XOR decryption.

Challenge 03 — antioch (1,885,074 bytes). Monty Python and the Holy Grail reference ('Holy Hand Grenade of Antioch'). Likely a Docker/container-based challenge where participants navigate a custom environment. Technique class: container analysis / custom runtime.

metadata.technique_class: Docker container / custom runtime analysis (Monty Python theme)

artifacts.description: Challenge 04 — myaquaticlife (2,369,123 bytes). Aquatic-themed game or simulation. Likely a .NET or game binary where aquatic-themed logic conceals a key derivation puzzle. Technique class: game reversing / .NET decompilation.

Challenge 05 — FLARE_Linux_VM (321,916,242 bytes). Dominant artifact at 322 MB — a full Linux virtual machine image. Participants must forensically analyze the live system to find the flag. This is an OS-level forensics challenge requiring Linux artifact analysis (bash history, cron, /proc, systemd, etc.). Technique class: Linux forensics / VM image analysis.

metadata.technique_class: Linux VM image / OS-level forensics / live system analysis

artifacts.description: Challenge 06 — PetTheKitty (675,952 bytes). Network challenge. 'Pet the kitty' likely refers to a SYN-ACK keepalive pattern or a network packet sequence that must be replicated or decoded. Technique class: network protocol analysis / PCAP reversing.

metadata.technique_class: network protocol analysis / PCAP / keepalive sequence

artifacts.description: Challenge 07 — spel (1,041,938 bytes). 'Spel' is Swedish/Dutch for 'game' and also an anagram of 'piles'. Likely an NES ROM or retro console game challenge requiring knowledge of the 6502 instruction set or custom emulator. Technique class: NES ROM / retro RE / 6502 assembly.

metadata.technique_class: NES ROM / retro console RE / 6502 assembly

artifacts.description: Challenge 08 — beelogin (325,746 bytes). JavaScript login form challenge. 'Beelogin' suggests a bee-themed HTML/JS page where the authentication logic is obfuscated in JavaScript. Technique class: JavaScript deobfuscation / browser-based credential reversing (T1059.007).

metadata.technique_class: JavaScript obfuscation / HTML login form reversing (T1059.007)

artifacts.description: Challenge 09 — evil (1,383,970 bytes). The name 'evil' directly signals an obfuscated or malicious sample for behavioral analysis. Likely an anti-analysis challenge (packing, VM detection, timing attacks). Technique class: malware analysis / anti-debug / VM evasion (T1027, T1564).

metadata.technique_class: malware analysis / anti-debug / VM evasion (T1027, T1564)

artifacts.description: Challenge 10 — wizardcult (3,856,291 bytes). Final boss challenge. 'Wizardcult' suggests a fantasy-themed multi-stage challenge with custom encryption, protocol reversing, or a complete malware ecosystem. Largest challenge by archive size (excl. VM). Technique class: complex multi-stage RE / custom cryptography / network protocol.

metadata.technique_class: multi-stage RE / custom crypto / complete malware ecosystem (final boss)

known_limitations: 7z archives were not extracted — individual challenge binaries were not hashed or analyzed.
All technique-class attributions are INFERRED from name, size, naming conventions, and FLARE-On 8 public write-ups, not from binary analysis.
7zip_password.txt was not read — the shared password is not recorded.
ch03 antioch technique class (Docker) is based on community knowledge that FLARE-On 8 ch03 used Docker; if this is incorrect the classification is INFERRED-LOW.
